items.title: Driver in fatal Gua Musang crash believed to be migrant smuggler
items.summary: GUA MUSANG: Police believe the driver of a Proton X70 involved in a crash that killed two people on Jalan Gua Musang-Kuala Lipis near Bukit Lanjut on Thursday was a migrant smuggler. District police chief Superintendent Sik Choon Foo said the driver, who was critically injured in the crash, is now in a coma and receiving treatment at Gua Musang Hospital. He said two migrants were killed while six others were injured.

items.title: As cyber threats strike at AI speed, Malaysia urged to embed risk‑based defence
items.summary: Telekom Malaysia Chief Information Security Officer Raja Azrina Raja Othman, who was among the co-founders of MyCERT in 1997, said cyber threats three decades ago were largely confined to specific systems and networks. Today, however, almost all services operate digitally and are interconnected, ranging from banking and government services to corporate operations and national critical infrastructure. “Cyber attackers today operate rapidly with the aid of AI.

items.title: Nepal authorities begin burying 229 unidentified bodies after floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Authorities in Nepal's Chitwan district began burying 229 unidentified bodies on Saturday due to public health risks from decomposition, following Wednesday's devastating floods in Rasuwa. The District Security Committee said 233 bodies had been recovered from the disaster so far, of which only four had been identified. The committee decided on Saturday to bury all the unidentified and unclaimed bodies under the Unidentified and Unclaimed Bodies Management (First Amendment) Directive, 2026, as an emergency measure to prevent further decomposition and ensure their safe, dignified and lawful disposal.

items.title: Nepal disaster: Families of Malaysians still unaccounted for to receive briefing tomorrow
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Families of Malaysians who remain unaccounted for following flash floods and landslides along the Nepal-Tibet border will be briefed by the Foreign Ministry, National Security Council (NSC) and relevant agencies tomorrow. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the meeting would provide the latest updates on efforts to locate the Malaysians who remain unaccounted for. He said Wisma Putra was operating a 24-hour operations room to monitor developments following the disaster and remained in constant contact with Nepal's Foreign Ministry, NSC and relevant agencies.

items.title: 11,060 Sahabat Madani volunteers join nationwide movement
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: A total of 11,060 Sahabat Madani volunteers have registered nationwide, forming a volunteer movement aimed at strengthening community ties and encouraging Malaysians from different ethnic, religious and social backgrounds to serve together. Earlier, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim launched the national Sahabat Madani initiative at the Ambang Merdeka Sahabat Madani 2026 highlight programme at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Permatang Pauh here. It said volunteer work across social differences could promote harmony and strengthen community ties, while bringing people together to tackle poverty, hardship, corruption and injustice.

items.title: Immigration to seek Thai details on syndicate trafficking China nationals from Cambodia into Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — The Immigration Department will work with Thai authorities to obtain detailed information on an alleged syndicate trafficking China nationals from Cambodia to Malaysia. “We will get further information from Thai authorities on this matter,” he said when contacted by Bernama today, after Thai media outlets reported that Thai authorities arrested two individuals suspected of being masterminds of a ring trafficking China nationals from the Cambodian border to Malaysia through Thailand. Thai authorities also identified four Thai nationals believed to be involved in the ring, including the individual arranging the immigrants’ journey from the Cambodia-Thai border to Hat Yai and onwards through to Malaysia.

items.title: Anwar: ‘Not a zero‑sum game’ as language mastery broadens unity and opportunity
items.summary: PERMATANG PAUH, Aug 29 — Efforts to uphold Malay, the country’s official language, should not be seen as an attempt to undermine proficiency in other languages, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said every citizen, regardless of racial background, should have a good command of the national language, while at the same time, proficiency in other languages such as English, Mandarin and Tamil should continue to be strengthened to broaden educational and economic opportunities. Elaborating, Anwar said proficiency in Mandarin was becoming increasingly important given its position as one of the region’s major economic languages, while Malaysians were also interested in improving their proficiency in Tamil.

items.title: Selangor looks to AI to boost govt services, efficiency
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Selangor is moving towards becoming an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered state, with AI set to be integrated into government operations and public services to improve efficiency. State Islamic Affairs and Digital Innovation Committee chairman Dr Mohammad Fahmi Ngah said the next phase of the state's Smart City agenda would focus on using data and AI to shape policies and improve services. Fahmi said the move would complete the Smart City cycle by allowing data collected through existing systems and applications to be analysed and translated into policies, regulations and guidelines.

items.title: Anwar extends Malaysia’s condolences to Norway on passing of King Harald V
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today extended condolences on behalf of the Malaysian government to the people of Norway on the passing of King Harald V. Anwar said King Harald would be remembered for his generous understanding of what it meant to be Norwegian, including his recognition of the country’s diverse society. Anwar said King Harald also understood the weight of an oath and the importance of remaining true to one’s commitments. “Malaysia joins the people of Norway in mourning his passing,” the Prime Minister said.

items.title: Rescuers push deeper into mudslide-hit areas at Xizang border post
items.summary: GYIRONG: Drones are scouting conditions as rescue teams advance on foot following a massive mudslide in Gyirong Port, southwest China's Xizang Region, where blocked roads and the risk of further disasters are hampering the search for hundreds of missing people, reported Xinhua. [[nid:1521390]] The National Fire and Rescue Administration has deployed 681 personnel, 13 rescue dogs, 113 vehicles, 47 drones and specialised equipment. MEM has also deployed 60 personnel and 28 pieces of equipment from a natural disaster rescue centre operated by China Anneng Group.

items.title: Maha 2026: Exhibition Hall A reopens after smoke incident
items.summary: SERDANG: Exhibition Hall A at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (Maeps) reopened this evening after being temporarily closed following an incident involving smoke and an unpleasant smell. In a statement, the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (Maha) 2026 organising committee said the incident at 4.50pm was brought under control after checks by the Fire and Rescue Department and the site's safety management team found no ongoing safety threat. The committee said the temporary evacuation of the hall was a standard precautionary measure under the Maha 2026 Safety Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) to ensure the safety and comfort of visitors and exhibitors.

items.title: Traffic flow on major highways congested following long weekend
items.summary: A spokesman for the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA) said traffic heading north was detected moving slowly from Sungai Buloh towards Bukit Beruntung, Bukit Tagar to Lembah Beringin, and Sungkai to Simpang Pulai. He said congestion to the north was also reported from Changkat Jering to Taiping Utara, Bukit Merah to Bandar Baharu and Permatang Pauh towards Bertam. "Meanwhile, southbound traffic flow was reported to be congested starting from Bangi towards Southville, and continuing from Nilai Utara extending to Pedas Linggi.

items.title: Subang Jaya police open investigation into viral Facebook claim against officers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Police have opened an investigation paper regarding a Facebook post that allegedly contained defamatory statements against police officers at a petrol station in Batu 14, Puchong, Selangor yesterday. Subang Jaya district police chief ACP Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said his department received a report from a police officer who was on duty at the time of the incident at 10.54pm. “The police have opened an investigation paper following the allegations under Section 500 of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.

items.title: Haze: Japan offers water-bombing aid as Kalimantan ISPU surges past 1,000
items.summary: National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) Acting Head of Data, Information and Disaster Communication Centre Berton Panjaitan said the assistance would involve three helicopters, including a Chinook, with operations scheduled to begin on Sept 10. Latest data from the Environment Ministry showed Jekan Raya in Palangka Raya, Central Kalimantan, recording an ISPU of 1,108 as of 4.55pm on Saturday, while Southeast Pontianak in West Kalimantan reached 1,075. BNPB also reported 9,242 hotspots across West, Central and South Kalimantan, with all three provinces recording increases.

items.title: MAHA Expo hall closed after smoke incident, visitors evacuated as safety checks carried out
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 29 — Exhibition Hall A (Hall A) at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (MAEPS) was temporarily closed today following a minor incident involving smoke and an unpleasant odour at 4.50pm. “To ensure the safety and comfort of everyone, members of the public and exhibitors in Hall A are advised to calmly evacuate the hall with immediate effect until further notice,” it said. It said Hall A would only be reopened after the authorities had confirmed that it was safe, adding that the safety of visitors, exhibitors and personnel remained the organisers’ top priority.

items.title: Police open investigation paper over post defaming personnel in Puchong
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have opened an investigation paper regarding a Facebook post that allegedly contained defamatory statements against police officers at a petrol station in Batu 14, Puchong, Selangor yesterday. Subang Jaya police chief assistant commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said they received a report from a policeman who was on duty at the time of the incident at 10.54pm. Wan Azlan said the post claimed that a police patrol vehicle blocked traffic while the personnel involved were allegedly waiting for food from a foreign trader at the petrol station without paying.

items.title: PM extends condolences to Norway over passing of King Harald V
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today extended condolences on behalf of the Malaysian government to the people of Norway on the passing of King Harald V. Anwar said King Harald would be remembered for his generous understanding of what it meant to be Norwegian, including his recognition of the country's diverse society. Anwar said King Harald also understood the weight of an oath and the importance of remaining true to one's commitments. "Malaysia joins the people of Norway in mourning his passing," the prime minister said.

items.title: GRS to lead seat talks, Hajiji says coalition preparing machinery ahead of GE16
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 29 — Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS), as the coalition leading the Sabah government, will take the lead in determining seat allocations with its government allies for the next general election, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. Hajiji, who is also Parti Gagasan Rakyat Sabah (PGRS) president, said the coalition would eventually discuss the distribution of parliamentary seats with parties currently in the state government, including Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Barisan Nasional (BN). Hajiji said the main consideration would be to field candidates capable of winning the election.

items.title: The names of 49 Malaysians and three Singaporeans still missing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The names of 49 Malaysians and three Singaporeans still missing following the Nepal-China border disaster have been released by their families. The list was compiled by the Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) group based on information gathered from the affected families and available travel documents. The names and ages provided by MASFIH are: Malaysians 1.

items.title: Anwar: Colonial‑era laws curbing student freedom must be abolished to realise true independence
items.summary: PERMATANG PAUH, Aug 29 — Colonial-era laws restricting students’ freedom should be abolished to allow the true meaning of independence to be fully realised, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said university students should have more freedom to voice their views and take part in activities, as they would play a key role in shaping the country’s future. “That is why I announced last week that we would abolish university laws that restrict student activities.

items.title: Families cling on to hope after Nepal-Tibet border disaster
items.summary: Among the 75 family members gathered today in Batu Caves was Jamaliah Tengku Ismail, who said she was trying to balance hope with the possibility of bad news about her 68-year-old husband, Wan Nasir Abdul Talib. Jamaliah said he called her during the journey, but she missed the call. "As long as there is no other news, no news is still good news.

items.title: A Merdeka memory, made for the front page
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Under the scorching afternoon sun at Dataran Merdeka, visitors streamed through the historic square, watching parade rehearsals, taking photographs and soaking up the festivities ahead of National Day. Given a choice of newspapers for his personalised front page, he picked the New Straits Times. "Many people don't read newspapers anymore.

items.title: GRS to continue cooperation with PH, BN, says Hajiji
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) will continue its cooperation with its existing allies, said its chairman Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. "Currently, the Sabah state government is led by GRS. The full list is as follows: Kudat : Datuk Seri Ruddy Awah Kota Marudu : Saripin Magana Kota Belud : Datuk Mohd Arsad Bistari Tuaran : Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor Sepanggar : Datuk Mohamed Razali Mohamed Razi Kota Kinabalu : Datuk Faisyal YH Diego Putatan : Shah Alfie Yahya Ahmad Shah Penampang : Datuk Ceasar Mandela Malakun Papar : Datuk Gulamhaidar Khan Bahadar Kimanis : Datuk Dr Mohd Arifin Mohd Arif Beaufort : Datuk Isnin Aliasnih Sipitang : Datuk Dr Yusof Yacob Ranau : Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun Keningau : Datuk Azaman Ruslan Tenom : Datuk Rubin Balang Pensiangan : Datuk Abdul Ghani Yassin Beluran : Datuk James Ratib Libaran : Datuk Hazem Mubarak Tun Musa Batu Sapi : Datuk George Hiew Vun Zin Sandakan : Datuk Awang Kadin Tang Kinabatangan : Datuk Masiung Banah Lahad Datu : Rajesh Yusof Semporna : Datuk Dr Mohd Jasmin Julpin Tawau : Datuk Nizam Abu Bakar Titingan Kalabakan : Dr Andi Md Shamsureezal Mohd Sainal © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Traffic crawls along 20km stretch entering Kelantan as school break and National Day surge builds
items.summary: Gua Musang district police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said traffic police personnel and the Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) unit have been deployed to the location to conduct regular patrols. “Police are closely monitoring traffic flow along all major routes to ensure the safety and smooth movement of road users. However, he said traffic flow returned to normal after passing the diversion area.

items.title: Anwar: Learn English, Chinese, Tamil beyond mastering Bahasa Melayu
items.summary: PERMATANG PAUH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said proficiency in Bahasa Melayu should remain essential for Malaysians, while learning other languages could open up greater educational and economic opportunities. He said Malaysians should be encouraged to learn English, Chinese, Tamil and other languages while maintaining proficiency in Bahasa Melayu. "We must be proficient in Bahasa Melayu, but we can also learn English, Chinese, Tamil and other languages," he said.

items.title: Air quality worsens, two Sarawak stations breach very unhealthy levels, 29 areas nationwide unhealthy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Two monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today, while 29 other areas nationwide registered unhealthy air quality. An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy), and above 300 (hazardous). API figures are updated hourly based on readings from 68 monitoring stations nationwide.

items.title: Kopmedia ranks among KL's top 50 cooperatives
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Koperasi Media Prima Bhd (Kopmedia) has been ranked 46th among the 50 best-performing cooperatives in the Federal Territory under the 2026 Majlis Apresiasi Gerakan Koperasi Wilayah Persekutuan (MAGK'26). A total of 55 cooperatives received recognition at the event, comprising the 50 best cooperatives, two premier cooperatives and three special award recipients. He said five of the seven premier cooperatives were also from the Federal Territory, while 80 of the 1,200 cooperatives in the territory recorded annual income exceeding RM5 million and were categorised as large-cluster cooperatives.

items.title: Families of 49 Malaysians, three Singaporeans missing in Nepal-China flood disaster plead for answers [WATCH]
items.summary: The group said that it represented families of 49 Malaysians and three Singaporeans travelling in three separate groups whose whereabouts remained unknown. They said their loved ones were not among the 38 Malaysians Wisma Putra had reportedly said yesterday that it had established contact with. MASFIH said the 52 travellers the families are highlighting comprise 23 Malaysians and three Singaporeans travelling with Leaf Holiday, nine Malaysians linked to the Dream Tibet Travel and Tours group, and 17 Malaysians travelling with Fishtail Tours and Travels.

items.title: Street artist keeps old KL alive through Merdeka memories
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: As the Ambang Merdeka Festival 2026 approaches this weekend near historic Dataran Merdeka, street artist Mahadzir Jam is preserving memories of an older Kuala Lumpur through his art. Using acrylic markers, he paints colourful landscapes of traditional village houses, coconut trees and greenery on small canvases, magnets and other souvenirs, many marked "Kuala Lumpur" for tourists seeking a keepsake from the capital. "Kuala Lumpur has changed a lot.

items.title: Anwar vows to put rakyat's wellbeing ahead of personal gain
items.summary: PERMATANG PAUH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he would continue prioritising the wellbeing of the rakyat if given the opportunity to lead the country. Speaking at the Sahabat Madani 2026 Merdeka Eve programme at UiTM Permatang Pauh here today, Anwar said his focus was to ensure Malaysia remained stable while improving the lives and prospects of its people. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said he remained firm in rejecting corruption, abuse of power and attempts to use positions of authority for personal gain.

items.title: PH ready to begin Melaka seat talks with BN
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan (PH) is ready to begin seat negotiations with Barisan Nasional (BN) for the Melaka election, but talks are pending several policy decisions at the Umno and BN central level. PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said he had been in contact with Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, who told him he was awaiting the decisions before proceeding with the discussions. He said PH had previously demonstrated its willingness to compromise, including allowing BN to contest some seats won by PH in Selangor.

items.title: Floods: Nepal reverses decision to reject foreign rescue assistance
items.summary: MOSCOW: The Nepalese government has reversed its earlier decision to reject assistance from other countries in rescue operations following devastating floods that claimed hundreds of lives, amid "pressure" from other states, according to the Kathmandu Post newspaper, citing a senior government official, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti. On Friday, Nepalese Foreign Ministry spokesman Lok Bahadur Chhetri said Nepal did not need foreign assistance for search and rescue operations following the flooding. Previously, the United Nations (UN), the European Union (EU) and several countries had provided financial assistance to Nepal amid the destruction caused by the major flooding.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar: Colonial-era laws must go to give true meaning to independence
items.summary: PERMATANG PAUH: Colonial-era laws should be abolished to ensure Malaysia truly gives meaning to its independence, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar said independence was not merely about ending foreign rule, but also about reclaiming Malaysians' right to determine their own destiny, systems and future. They decided for us," he said.

items.title: Haze: Sri Aman, Serian record very unhealthy API readings
items.summary: Sri Aman's Air Pollutant Index (API) rose from 227 at 11am to 240 at 5pm. Similarly, Serian recorded an API reading of 228, up from 204 this morning. Five other districts in Sarawak also recorded higher "unhealthy" readings.

items.title: ‘We can only pray’: Family of missing Malaysian in Nepal tragedy anxiously awaits news
items.summary: Mures, 40, said his father’s journey to perform a religious ceremony on Mount Kailash, Tibet turned into a terrifying nightmare for the family after he was last seen active on the WhatsApp application on the morning of the incident. “My father alone joined a group with 16 other Malaysians to Mount Kailash in Tibet, China to perform a religious ceremony. He said the family had contacted various parties to obtain the latest information including the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu and the police.

items.title: Six Sukhois, three Airbus aircraft to highlight Melaka National Day
items.summary: MELAKA: Six Sukhoi fighter jets will headline this year's state-level National Day celebration at Dataran 1Malaysia, Klebang, with the public also able to view Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) assets and capabilities. Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said three Airbus air transport aircraft would also fly over Melaka, while six Royal Malaysian Navy (RMN) warships would be open for public viewing. Ab Rauf also said 15 tourist attractions across Melaka would offer free admission to the public on Aug 31.

items.title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning for KL, Selangor and five states until 7pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has warned of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in six states and Kuala Lumpur until 7pm today. MetMalaysia said the warning covered the entire state of Kelantan and 11 districts in Perak: Batang Padang, Muallim, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Perak Tengah, Larut Matang, Selama, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk. The warning also covers Hulu Terengganu, Dungun, Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Kuala Terengganu and Marang in Terengganu, as well as Lipis, Cameron Highlands, Rompin, Raub, Bentong, Jerantut and Temerloh in Pahang.

items.title: Haze: Asthma, conjunctivitis cases on the rise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Asthma cases in the country have surged amid deteriorating air quality caused by the haze affecting several areas nationwide, with 1,811 cases recorded during epidemiological week (EW) 34 (Aug 23-29), compared with 219 cases in the previous week. It said cases of conjunctivitis also rose to 720 from 146 in EW 33, while acute respiratory tract infections (URTI) fell by 50 per cent, from 3,674 to 1,857 cases. On air quality, the MOH said 30 of the 68 Air Pollutant Index (API) monitoring stations recorded unhealthy or very unhealthy readings as of 8am today, with Sri Aman, Sarawak recording the highest reading of 222, classified as very unhealthy.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms and heavy rain in six states and KL until 7pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has warned of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in seven states and Kuala Lumpur until 7pm today. MetMalaysia said the warning was issued for the entire state of Kelantan and 11 districts in Perak: Batang Padang, Muallim, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Perak Tengah, Larut Matang, Selama, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk. The warning also covers Hulu Terengganu, Dungun, Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Kuala Terengganu and Marang in Terengganu, and Lipis, Cameron Highlands, Rompin, Raub, Bentong, Jerantut and Temerloh in Pahang.

items.title: Wajah Malaysia puts Malaysians in the picture
items.summary: Currently stationed at Dataran Merdeka alongside Festival Ambang Merdeka 2026, the truck allows visitors to step into the photobooth and see themselves featured on a personalised mock front page of the New Straits Times, Berita Harian or Harian Metro. NSTP head of Branding and Intellectual Property Tengku Kaifimirza Tuan Cherit@Tengku Hamzah said the campaign provided an opportunity to engage with Malaysians, particularly younger visitors gathering at Dataran Merdeka. Visitors will also receive copies of NSTP newspapers, with 900 copies distributed daily — 300 each of the New Straits Times, Berita Harian and Harian Metro.

items.title: Malaysia's bonsai industry poised for global growth, says Nga
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's pool of world-class bonsai expertise represents a significant and largely untapped opportunity to elevate the craft beyond a recreational pastime into a more professional and commercially viable industry, capitalising on rising international demand. Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the country already possessed all the foundational elements required to transform bonsai into a high-value economic activity. Speaking on the sector's potential, Nga said that under the National Landscape Industry Master Plan, Malaysia's bonsai and landscape industry currently generates an estimated RM40 billion in annual economic value, with strong prospects for further expansion.

items.title: Nepal floods: 55 Malaysians still uncontactable - Wisma Putra
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Fifty-five Malaysians remain uncontactable following the floods and landslides that struck Rasuwa District, Nepal on Aug 26, according to Malaysia's Foreign Ministry. "Two Malaysians previously reported as uncontactable have since been contacted, and verification of the remaining cases is ongoing," the ministry, widely known as Wisma Putra, said in its latest statement updating the situation in Nepal and surrounding areas. The Embassy of Malaysia in Kathmandu continues to work with the Emergency Response Team of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Nepal, the Nepal Tourism Board, travel agencies and relevant local authorities.

items.title: Anwar says Malaysia’s success must be anchored by a knowledgeable, disciplined generation
items.summary: BATU KAWAN, Aug 29 — A country’s success should not be measured solely by economic and technological progress, but must also be supported by the development of a knowledgeable and disciplined younger generation, said Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The Prime Minister said young people should be provided with an education that also instils values, a spirit of service and a sense of responsibility towards their families, society and country. Also present were Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow and Chief Scout Datuk Prof Dr Mohd Zin Bidin.

items.title: Desa ParkCity family tragedy takes new turn as police reveal illegal investment issue alongside alleged love scam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Police investigating the deaths of a family of four at a Desa ParkCity condominium in Kepong have revealed that the couple had also become entangled in an illegal investment scheme, adding a new dimension to a case already linked to an alleged love scam and RM260,000 in losses and debt. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said relatives of the couple were aware of both issues. “The family knew about the love scam problem and that they had become trapped in an illegal investment scheme.

items.title: Wisma Putra: 55 Malaysians still uncontactable as checks expand to Nepal–China border areas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Fifty-five Malaysians remain uncontactable following the floods and landslides that struck Rasuwa District, Nepal on August 26, according to Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry. “Two Malaysians previously reported as uncontactable have since been contacted, and verification of the remaining cases is ongoing,” the ministry, widely known as Wisma Putra, said in its latest statement updating the situation in Nepal and surrounding areas. The Embassy of Malaysia in Kathmandu continues to work with the Emergency Response Team of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Nepal, the Nepal Tourism Board, travel agencies and relevant local authorities.

items.title: Nearly RM250,000 payout after Segambut jogger fractures spine while fending off neighbour’s German Shepherds
items.summary: Sinar Harian reported that KL Sessions Court judge Zawiyah Saad found Datuk Seri Ong Thiam Boon liable for the February 10, 2021 incident involving his neighbour, Datuk Mohd Kamal Abdullah. The court awarded Mohd Kamal RM178,457.60 in special damages and RM70,000 in general damages after a full trial. Ong, however, denied that the dogs had attacked or even come into contact with Mohd Kamal.

items.title: BNM warns of scammers using phone numbers similar to STR, Sara hotlines and impersonating MoF officials
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 29 — Members of the public have been advised to remain vigilant against individuals impersonating officials from the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) programmes. Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM), in issuing the warning, said some criminal groups had resorted to using telephone numbers similar to official hotlines to contact members of the public and gain their trust before obtaining their personal and banking information. The central bank appealed to the public not to disclose any personal or banking information to unidentified callers, including their MyKad number, bank account number, One-Time Password (OTP) or Transaction Authorisation Code (TAC), online banking password or Personal Identification Number (PIN), and other personal and financial information.

items.title: Pakatan open to Bersatu tie-up for Melaka state election as Amirudin says ‘that is politics’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is open to working with Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia in the coming Melaka state election, Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said, signalling that even former political adversaries could become potential partners as parties manoeuvre ahead of the polls. “Bersatu? PAS has also worked with Bersatu, PAS has separated from Bersatu, PAS has separated from Umno, and PAS has wanted to work with Umno.

items.title: Printer apologises, says last-minute order led to incorrect Jalur Gemilang star worn by Kedah MB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — A printing company has blamed a rushed last-minute order and less thorough quality checks for an incorrect Jalur Gemilang star appearing on attire worn by Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor and several dignitaries at a Merdeka event. The Ayer Keroh, Melaka-based company said an error during production resulted in the star on the printed Malaysian flag having fewer than the official 14 points. The company said it would immediately provide replacement attire that complied with the official specifications of the Jalur Gemilang.

items.title: Parents must caution teens that mule accounts can lead to legal action, says Ewon
items.summary: Sabah Deputy Chief Minister III Datuk Ewon Benedick, who is also Industrial Development, Entrepreneurship and Transport Minister, said allowing others to use their bank accounts could expose account holders to legal action if the accounts were found to have been used for fraud or other unlawful transactions. “Digital technology is now part of our daily lives. Ewon, who is also Penampang Member of Parliament, said digital technology had changed how people carried out various activities, including financial transactions, business dealings and applications for government assistance.

items.title: Amirudin tells Umno to ‘look in the mirror’ over sincerity in election seat talks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — PKR election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has pushed back against Umno’s call for sincerity in future election negotiations, saying Barisan Nasional (BN) should first examine its own approach after Pakatan Harapan (PH) previously gave up seats it had won to accommodate its unity government partner. Utusan Malaysia reported that Amirudin said negotiations would become difficult if one side imposed conditions before discussions had even begun. “Don’t impose conditions before discussions have even begun.

items.title: Desa ParkCity deaths: Post-mortems show two children were stabbed in the neck, mother suffered sharp-force wounds, says KL police chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Two children found dead with their parents at a Desa ParkCity home were killed by stab wounds to the neck, post-mortem examinations have confirmed. Berita Harian reported that Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said their mother, 47, meanwhile, died from sharp-force trauma to the neck and chest. “The post-mortem found that the cause of death was sharp-force trauma to the neck and chest,” Fadil said.

items.title: Putrajaya comes alive as National Day 2026 full rehearsal gets under way
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — Dataran Putrajaya came alive with uniformed contingents, Jalur Gemilang and the roar of national assets during today’s full rehearsal for the 2026 National Day celebrations. Beginning at 8 am, the rehearsal provided a preview of Monday’s celebrations, featuring corporate and government-linked companies (GLCs) and colourful special performances. — Bernama pic Among the highlights of the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) rehearsal was a human graphic performance involving 1,500 students from 36 schools in Selangor.

items.title: Durian, pineapple and RM8b in deals: Malaysia goes big at MAHA 2026
items.summary: Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said about RM4 billion of the total would involve partnerships with China, while the remainder would involve other countries. He said the agreements would cover technology exchange, investment opportunities, capacity building and training for farmers, including Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), as well as creating opportunities for local agri-food products to enter export markets. He added that the MAHA Go Global initiative would also help expand the reach of local products, particularly in Central Asia and Eastern Europe.

items.title: Jendela Phase Two to begin at 1,000 sites nationwide this year, says deputy minister
items.summary: KULAI, Aug 29 — A total of 1,000 sites, including in Sabah and Sarawak, have been identified for the implementation of Phase Two of the National Digital Network (Jendela) plan this year, said Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching. She said its implementation would ensure stronger and more stable internet coverage nationwide. She said free public transport facilities, including shuttle buses, would also be provided at MRT Putrajaya Sentral every five minutes, while services at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre would operate every 10 minutes.

items.title: More than 2,300 police deployed for National Day celebrations in Putrajaya
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — A total of 2,354 members and officers of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have been assigned to ensure the highest level of security and smooth running of the 2026 National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya on Monday. Aidi Sham also reminded the public not to bring any dangerous weapons when attending the National Day celebration. Earlier, Fahmi said the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya on August 31, will so far be held as usual, Themed “ Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati ”, the 69th National Day celebration will be held at Dataran Putrajaya with an expectation of more 80,000 visitors coming to witness the historic day.

items.title: Fire destroys 60pc of Pos Laju building in Bekenu, no injuries reported
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — A fire destroyed about 60 per cent of a Pos Laju building in Bekenu, about 47km south-west of Miri in Sarawak, this morning, although no one was injured. The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department’s Operations Centre said in a statement today that it received an emergency call at 8.44am before five firefighters from the Batu Niah Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene. The team, led by Senior Fire Officer II Azalan Azaman, arrived at about 9.30am and found the Pos Laju building, measuring about 15.2m by 12.2m, on fire.

items.title: Mask up for Merdeka: National Day crowds urged to wear N95s amid haze
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — Visitors to the 2026 National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya this Monday are advised to wear N95 masks to protect themselves from the effects of the current haze. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, who is also National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) 2026 celebrations main committee chairman, said the advice was in line with recommendations issued by the Health Ministry (MOH), particularly for high-risk individuals. He said the organisers of the 2026 HKHM celebrations were also providing N95 masks to more than 10,000 participants as a precautionary measure to safeguard their health.

items.title: Going to Dataran Putrajaya for National Day celebrations? Free water taxis are available from 5am on Aug 31
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — Members of the public who wish to attend the 2026 National Day Celebration at Dataran Putrajaya on August 31 are urged to take advantage of the free water transport facilities provided by the Putrajaya Corporation (PPj) to facilitate movement to the celebration location. “This year in conjunction with National Day on August 31, the Putrajaya Corporation (PPj) is providing a free water taxi service starting at 5am until 2pm on August 31,” he told Bernama after reviewing the operational preparations for the service here today. Based on PPj information, the free water transportation service covers the cruise taxi route between Marina Putrajaya and Anjung Floria as well as between Kelab Tasik Putrajaya and Monumen.

items.title: Man, 49, held in murder probe after five-year-old boy dies in Sibu
items.summary: Sibu police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said the suspect was remanded until September 4 following a remand application at the Sibu Magistrates’ Court today. Following information received, police arrested the 49-year-old suspect believed to be involved in the incident. Abang Zainal said several items believed to be connected to the case were also seized at the scene.
